research_summary: A log-years ladder: an adult mayfly (~a day), the average person (73.3 yr), the oldest tortoise (~193 yr), the Greenland shark (~392 +/- 120 yr), the oldest non-clonal tree (~4,850 yr), the Sun (~10 billion yr), a red dwarf (~4 trillion yr), and the proton (never seen to decay; lower limits above 1e33 yr). The honest twist: the longest rung is a limit nobody has reached, so 'forever' stays a MAYBE.

data_points.claim: Adult mayflies live from ~30 minutes to 1-2 days depending on species; 'about a day' is typical. PROBABLY (varies by species) [MAYFLY]
Global life expectancy at birth was 73.3 years in 2023 (WHO Global Health Estimates, Oct 2026). MEASURED [HUMAN]
Jonathan, a Seychelles/Aldabra giant tortoise on St Helena, hatched ~1832: age ~193-194 in 2026; oldest known living land animal (Guinness). PROBABLY (hatch year estimated) [TORTOISE]
Greenland shark: largest animal (502 cm) aged 392 +/- 120 years by eye-lens radiocarbon; range 272-512 yr; longest-lived known vertebrate (Nielsen et al., Science 2016). PROBABLY [SHARK]

Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine in California, is ~4,789-4,856 years old (Guinness 4,856 in 2024); oldest known non-clonal tree; its age has not been independently reproduced (missing core). PROBABLY [PINE]
Sun: ~4.6 billion years old, about halfway through a ~10 billion year main-sequence life (NASA). PROBABLY (stellar model) [SUN]
Red dwarfs burn hydrogen so slowly that Proxima Centauri is expected to stay on the main sequence ~4 trillion years (smaller ones up to ~10 trillion). PROBABLY (stellar model) [DWARF]
No proton decay has ever been observed; Super-Kamiokande sets lower limits on the proton lifetime of 3.6e33 yr (p -> mu+ K0) and 5.9e33 yr (p -> nu K+) at 90% CL. MEASURED (a lower limit) [PROTON]
Some grand unified theories predict proton decay near 1e34-1e36 yr; whether protons decay at all is unknown. MAYBE [FOREVER]

1e33 is a 1 followed by 33 zeros; spoken, a billion trillion trillion (1e9 x 1e24). The ZEROS counter shows the power of ten of each rung (mayfly 0, you 1, tortoise 2, shark 2, pine 3, Sun 10, dwarf 12, proton 33). MEASURED (arithmetic) [ZEROS]

common_questions: What is the oldest living thing?

misconceptions.myth: The Greenland shark is known to be 500 years old
misconceptions.reality: 392 +/- 120 years is a radiocarbon estimate; 512 is the upper end of the range, not a measured age.

misconceptions.myth: Protons are known to last forever
misconceptions.reality: No decay has been seen, which only sets a lower limit of ~1e33 years; theory leaves open that they decay.
